claim_status: Exact continuous obstruction for weighted C5 blow-ups only. This does not solve Erdős #128.
statement: For every weighted blow-up of C5 with part weights x_i >= 0 and sum x_i = 1, there is a fractional half-subgraph with C5 edge density at most 1/50. The balanced blow-up attains equality.
proof: Let z_i = x_i + x_{i+2}, indices modulo 5.
If some z_i >= 1/2, take half the mass from the two nonadjacent parts i and i+2; this gives edge density 0.
Otherwise z_i < 1/2 for every i. For each i, take all mass from parts i and i+2 and fill delta_i = 1/2 - z_i from a neighbour of the smaller of x_i and x_{i+2}.
The resulting half-subgraph has edge density h_i = delta_i * min(x_i, x_{i+2}).
Since min(x_i, x_{i+2}) <= z_i/2, h_i <= z_i*(1/2-z_i)/2.
If h_i > 1/50 for every i, then z_i*(1/2-z_i)/2 > 1/50 for every i. By the exact factorization h(z)-1/50 = -1/2*(z-1/10)*(z-2/5), this forces z_i < 2/5 for every i.
But sum_i z_i = 2*sum_i x_i = 2, so the average z_i is 2/5. The strict inequalities z_i < 2/5 for all i contradict this.
Therefore some constructed half-subgraph has edge density at most 1/50.

scope.rules_out: Any asymptotic counterexample to #128 obtained solely as a weighted C5 blow-up with threshold strictly above 1/50.
scope.does_not_rule_out: Non-C5 triangle-free graphs, finite rounding effects, or a different structural construction.
